conditions: Only Unicode apostrophe glyphs are normalized to ASCII apostrophe.
The apostrophe is retained as an internal token character.
Match only a listed contraction with its exact auxiliary expansion.
Use a contiguous 1↔2 token span and preserve all surrounding tokens, order, and polarity.
The expansion must be unique for that contraction.

modeConditions.vocabulary: Align only to the existing canonical/answers/source authority; paraphrases remain PARAPHRASE.
modeConditions.read: Match only the complete contiguous pair in order; preserve every other reference token and highlight reference indexes from the alignment.
modeConditions.cloze: The entire hidden target must be reproduced in place by the selected final utterance; all completeness and negation gates remain mandatory.
modeConditions.correction: Use the complete pair only; correction practice adds no scheduled SRS write.

conditions: Resolve ’s as is or has only when the complete local syntax admits exactly one standard parse.
Treat be + -ing and ’s been/’s got as candidate clues, not universal morphology rules.
Past-participle/adjective, ’s not, nominal, and possession collisions remain unresolved absent a complete parse.

excludedModes.read: UNRESOLVED: context-dependent auxiliary parsing is outside the bounded exact-span policy.
excludedModes.cloze: UNRESOLVED: context-dependent auxiliary parsing is outside the hidden-target policy.

conditions: Resolve ’d as had before an unambiguously past participle, or would before an unambiguously bare infinitive / fixed better-rather idiom.
Keep syncretic forms such as put, read, and cut unresolved without wider syntax.
Do not infer elided have in would have constructions.
Match only the exact listed auxiliary + not pair and its listed contraction.
The aligned span must contain the auxiliary and the negative marker together.
Preserve auxiliary identity, tense, order, and negation scope in both directions.

modeConditions.vocabulary: Align only to existing canonical/answers/source authority; a paraphrase is never promoted.
modeConditions.read: Match the complete auxiliary + negator pair contiguously and preserve the remainder of the reference.
modeConditions.cloze: The complete hidden target span must map in place; preservesExpectedNegation and completeness remain hard gates.
modeConditions.correction: Match the complete pair; do not add a scheduled SRS write.

conditions: Treat cannot/can’t as a listed fixed negative pair.
Do not automatically equate can not with cannot/can’t: split can not may scope over the following verb or express a choice not to act.

excludedModes.cloze: UNRESOLVED pending scope and target policy.

conditions: Resolve let’s to let us only as a first-person plural hortative with a following base verb.
Do not equate with permission/request “let us …” without discourse evidence.
No automatic expansion. A dialect-specific speaker model and sentence parse would be required.
Do not expand lexical ’s as an auxiliary when followed by a possessed noun.
Any possessive/auxiliary collision requires complete syntax and reference context.
The complete phrase uses ’s as a possessive determiner before a lexical noun.
Do not expand it to be/have or strip the possessive relation.
Require context-specific lexical/grammatical evidence for were/we’re, your/you’re, their/they’re/there, and its/it’s.
Do not infer an apostrophe or auxiliary from sound alone.
Aren’t I is eligible only as the conventional negative tag after a first-person positive clause.
It is not a general spelling/contraction of am not.
Negation marker and scope must be preserved in both directions.
Auxiliary, tense/aspect, and modal force must remain the same.
A contracted auxiliary must be licensed by its syntactic construction; do not assume an elided predicate at sentence end.
Accept a short answer only if that exact elliptical form is independently licensed.
Evaluate each finalized hypothesis independently.
Do not join words from rank 0, lower ranks, segments, or prior attempts.
